# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 56 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 56 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_056_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 2 — First Interpretation: The Flesh and the Holy Spirit

**56:1** I asked him to explain the parable to me. "What are you asking to understand?" he said. "Lord," I replied, "why was the son's inheritance not sufficient for the slave? Why was he established as co-heir with the son?"

**56:2** "Listen," he said. "The slave who kept the lord's commandment and instruction — he is the holy spirit who dwelt in the flesh. And his flesh served this spirit well, walking in holiness and purity, not defiling the spirit in any way."

**56:3** "When therefore this flesh had conducted itself so well and purely, and had labored together with the spirit and cooperated with it in everything, conducting itself with valor and fortitude, he chose it as a partner with the holy spirit. For the conduct of this flesh pleased the Lord, in that it had not been defiled while bearing the holy spirit upon the earth."

**56:4** "He took the son and the trustworthy slaves as counselors. These are the holy angels who were created first. The master took counsel with them to the effect that this flesh — having served the holy spirit blamelessly — should have some resting place, lest it should appear to have lost the reward of its service."

**56:5** "For every flesh in which the holy spirit has dwelt shall receive a reward, if it is found undefiled and spotless. This, then, is the interpretation of this parable as well."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the pneumatological-christological argument of the parable's interpretation.*
